data.title: The Cornerstone's Twin
data.rumour: The marina dig on Harbor Green hit a granite block with a date on it.
data.teaser: There's a chain-link fence round half of Harbor Green, and a sign: FUTURE HOME OF HAINES HARBOR MARINA. A BIG SHINY THING FOR HOLLOW NECK.
about: A March chapter of Spoons, after the spoons went to Delphine Rook. Gordie's marina dig on Harbor Green hits a 1904 granite block under the bandstand with seven brass dials, the Athenaeum cornerstone's twin (§{twinGus}). Rook lends you the seven spoons that open it, for first refusal on whatever's inside (§{twinRook}).

At night in the rain (§{twinNight}) the spoons open it, and inside is a covenant: if anyone ever sells the Green, the sale is void and the Green returns, in trust for the town, to whoever holds the paper. Gordie offers $300. Give it to Hester for the town, which stops the marina (The People's Green), sell it to Gordie, who tears it up (Breaking Ground), or take it to Ellery Thorne, whose grandfather wrote it (In His Good Hat).

greenCovenant.name: The Harbor Green covenant, 1904
tells: "Should any person ever sell this Green, the sale is void, and the Green returns to whoever holds this paper, in trust for the town." Signed J. Thorne, witnessed by the whole Old Home Week committee.

twinGus.title: Gus and the granite under the bandstand

text: Gus Lindqvist. The chess tables on the Green. You'll have seen the fence. Gordie's marina. They dug up my tables on Monday. They said sorry.
Then the backhoe hit granite under the bandstand and stopped. A block, like a cornerstone. A.D. 1904, OLD HOME WEEK. And seven little dials on the side.
Hester says the Athenaeum's cornerstone had a twin, in the minutes. Hester says you know about spoons.

twinRook.title: Delphine Rook still has the spoons

text: Delphine Rook. I hear the Green has a second box in it. I still have the seven spoons, of course. I never sell a set. I only ever sell what's inside.
I'll lend them to you for the night. In return, whatever's in the box, I get first refusal. That's all. I'm very reasonable for a woman with seven spoons.

then.text: Lovely. I'll bring them myself. I've brought a thermos to everything else.

choose.label: "Gordie's paying for the dig. Lend them to him."

then.text: Gordie would melt them down for the marina sign. No, I'll bring them. You can watch.

steps.text: The contractor will open it for us {placed:twin-night} night, after his crew's gone home.

steps.toast: Calendar: Harbor Green, the second cornerstone, {placed:twin-night} night

steps.narrate: Harbor Green after dark, in the March rain, under two contractor's lights on poles. The bandstand is jacked up on timbers. Under it, in a hole full of meltwater, is a granite block with seven brass dials.

steps.text: Tuck Moreau, I drive the backhoe. I'm not touching it. My grandmother would come back and slap me.
Gordie Haines! Selectman or not, it's my Green now, I've got the deed. Whatever's in there is mine, legally. Probably. Open it.

narrate: Rook lays the spoons on a clean handkerchief in the 1904 order and reads them off to you: one, nine, zero, four, one, seven, six. The dials are stiff with a hundred and twenty years of the Green. The block slides out on its runners.

Inside, a lead box, and inside that, one folded paper and a photograph: the whole Old Home Week committee on this bandstand in 1904, in straw hats, every one of them looking straight at the camera, as if they knew.

steps.text: "Should any person ever sell this Green, the sale is void, and the Green returns to whoever holds this paper, in trust for the town." Oh, that's wicked. J.T. knew about people like me.
That's a piece of paper. I've got a piece of paper too. Mine's got a notary on it. Three hundred dollars says yours goes in the dumpster with the bandstand.

choose.label: Give the covenant to Hester Quint for the town

then.narrate: Hester takes it in the morning, in a plastic sleeve, to the town clerk and then to a lawyer in Plymouth who used to be her student. By the end of the week the fence is down, and the marina is a drawing on the wall of Haines Motors.

then.text: You know what, fine. FINE. I'll put the marina on Pier Nine. It was always better on Pier Nine. I'm going to sell you a truck one day, and it's going to have a terrible radio.

then.why: Saved Harbor Green from the marina
Gordie Haines bought the Harbor Green covenant

then.narrate: Gordie counts out three hundred in twenties, tears the covenant in half, then in quarters, and drops the pieces in the meltwater. The photograph floats for a moment, face up, all those straw hats, and then it doesn't.

then.text: I said first refusal. I refuse. I'd have paid five.

choose.label: Take it up Cliff Road to Ellery Thorne

narrate: Ellery Thorne opens the door on Cliff Road in his dressing gown, sees who it is, and nearly shuts it. Then he sees what you're holding. He reads it on the doorstep, in the rain, without his glasses, because he doesn't need them for that handwriting.

In the morning he walks it down to Town Hall himself, in his good hat, and puts it in front of the town clerk, and doesn't leave until it's stamped. On the way out he nods to you across Main Street. It's the first time since October.

then.why: Ellery Thorne paid you for his grandfather's covenant

steps.note: whichever way, the covenant leaves your shelves

epilogue.line: Harbor Green belongs to the people forever, twice now. Gus Lindqvist's chess tables are back by the memorial. The bandstand has a new plaque with a photograph of men in straw hats.
Haines Harbor Marina opens on the Green in June. The jingle is already written. Delphine Rook has stopped bringing a thermos to things.
Ellery Thorne framed his grandfather's covenant next to the deed in the Athenaeum. He has started inviting people to dinner again, and one of them is you.

rumour: They're fencing off half the Green for Gordie's marina. My chess tables are on the wrong side of the fence. Forty years, those tables.
The digger hit something under the bandstand. Granite. Tuck Moreau stopped the machine and went home. Tuck doesn't stop for anything.

react.green: My tables are back by the memorial. The fence is gone. I played a game against Gordie Haines yesterday and let him win, which I have never done for anybody. I felt sorry for him.
react.marina: Gordie tore it up in a puddle, they say. A marina on the Green. I've moved my tables to the library steps. The pigeons are worse.
react.thorne: Ellery Thorne walked down Main Street in his good hat with a piece of paper, and the whole town stopped to watch. I haven't seen a man that pleased with himself since 1971, and that was me.
